newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold tumbles on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold tumbles on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong bullion tumbled on Thursday on across-the-board sales and gold was seen testing a year-low of $377, gold dealers and traders said.
Gold traders at banks and bullion houses in the British colony reported gold sales from Australian and South African producers, Japanese clients, U.S. funds and professionals.
Gold traded between highs of $380.35/65 and lows of $379.10/30 and was expected to test $377, dealers said.
U.S. funds were looking to push the market down in early morning trade, one gold trader said, while another noted speculative selling from Japanese clients.
South African producer hedge sales were more notable as the rand fell to all-time lows against the dollar on Thursday morning, industry sources said.
"South African miners are loving this, they're making a great profit," said one bullion dealer at an international bank's Hong Kong office.
The rand fell to an all-time low of 4.7670/7720 to the dollar early Thursday, boosting the price of gold in rand.
Gold dropped steadily from the opening until the afternoon when it registered a slight increase as physical demand in Hong Kong and the Asia Pacific kicked in, gold traders said.
"Demand has been quite huge today," said one gold trader.
Bullion ended at US$379.20/70 an ounce on Thursday against New York's US$380.15/55 close on Wednesday.
Local gold ended HK$12 lower at HK$3,496 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -6.00 from its previous fix at -3.00 BULLION -
